A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gauss–Newton optimization study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a complete comparison, including matching the renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 language-model training experiments, including optimizer comparisons, iteration complexity and batch-size scaling in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 6 and the renumbered Appendix G, including results for 45M- and 150M-parameter models.

M1.justification: The GN, GN-prox-linear and layerwise objectives and updates remain unchanged, including Muon inner optimization and line search. New Algorithm 3 documents computation of the existing inner objective and gradient; it does not establish a different optimization update.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4 language-model pretraining with the same task coverage. No dataset, domain or evaluation scenario is added or removed; the 45M-model experiments move from Appendix F to G.

E2.justification: AdamW, Muon and SOAP retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. The GN-prox-linear and layerwise comparisons also retain the same comparator membership in Figures 1–3 and 6.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Tables 1–3 retain the model configurations, context length, warmup, batch sizes, token budgets, target losses and hyperparameter sweeps. The implementation appendix introduces no reported change to experimental settings.

E4.justification: The higher-order-loss and layerwise-curvature comparisons, learning-rate schedule discussion and line-search analysis are retained. Figures 3–5 contain no added or revised ablation or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The revision introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Section 7 changes the stated slowdown relative to standard training from roughly 4–5× to 1.5×. No matched timing comparison accompanies this revision. Plotted results remain unchanged, including 54 GN, 78 layerwise-GN and 292 SOAP steps to loss 3.25 in Figure 1.

T1.justification: Appendix A makes a local algebraic correction by removing the Jacobian transpose from the expanded quadratic's linear term. Appendix B explicitly states the gradient used by the implementation. The equivalence result and formal assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal claims about iteration-complexity gains, improved batch-size scaling, sufficient layerwise curvature and limited benefit from higher-order loss terms are retained. The revision does not redefine the study's central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 narrows the stated computational-cost limitation from a 4–5× slowdown to 1.5×. The proof-of-concept framing, incomplete inner-optimization caveat and interpretations of layerwise curvature and higher-order loss terms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through a code-availability link and Appendix B's detailed inner-step pseudocode. Algorithm 3 specifies linearization, Jacobian-vector products, logit-space Hessian-vector products and gradient computation, filling a central implementation gap in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Hessian-free and approximate second-order optimization are unchanged. Additional Related Work is renumbered from Appendix B to C without substantive revision.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an implementation appendix, adds short code and implementation pointers, updates appendix cross-references and corrects local notation. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: The new appendix adds displayed equations and a formatted Algorithm 3 block, with limited reflow elsewhere. All six figures and three tables retain their visual structure, captions and content; existing appendix displays move with renumbering.

improvement.justification: The implementation appendix and code pointer improve transparency and make the central computation easier to reproduce. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the revised runtime overhead lacks an accompanying controlled timing comparison. The supported overall gain is therefore limited but useful.
